newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIA PIPELINE REPAIR WORK DELAYED.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIA PIPELINE REPAIR WORK DELAYED.

text.p: Repairs are complete on two sections of Colombia's crippled Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline but work has not yet started on a third break, oil industry sources said Friday.
A spokesman for state-run oil company Ecopetrol said it had been hoped all repairs would be completed by Friday night but the continued presence of leftist rebels had hindered operations.
Once work did begin it would take about 24 hours to fix the last section, he said.
The pipeline has been out of action for 10 days after a rebel dynamite attack on July 30. It was blown up twice more and partially destroyed by a landslide last weekend.

"Damage caused by one of the explosions and by the landslide have been repaired already but the army has still not authorized our engineers to begin repairing the third rupture because of the guerrilla threat," the spokesman said.
Occidental Petroleum Corp which operates the 175,000 barrel per day Cano Limon field, in northeast Arauca province, shut in production and declared force majeure Monday.
Ecopetrol declared force majeure on liftings at the Caribbean coast lifting terminal later in the week, delaying at least two shipments of 500,000 barrels each.

The Ecopetrol spokesman said crude supplies at Colombia's two main refineries in Barrancabermeja and Cartagena, which have a combined daily throughput of about 240,000 barrel per day, would have to be replenished before the force majeure on liftings could end.

Occidental is thought to have about 500,000 barrels of crude in storage on site at Cano Limon. Once the pipeline is repaired it could pump about 250,000 barrels per day in order to normalize stocks as soon as possible.
Output from the field cannot, however, be ramped up much beyond its daily average of 175,000 barrels.
